patients.summary: Healthy graduate student who joined in fall 2023, developed progressive dysmenorrhea and deep dyspareunia in 2024 and was diagnosed clinically with endometriosis by gynecology; she stays on over-the-counter NSAIDs. Last seen on a video visit in December 2024; in July 2026 an outside ED saw her for a transient low blood pressure episode during a research study.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 28 y/o grad student who moved to Belchertown for her program last year and has not had a local doctor since. Wants to sign up for membership and get a first physical in. Went over membership fee and that insurance still covers labs/specialists. Scheduled new patient physical 10/3 at 9:00. Emailed the records release for her old primary care office; she will sign and send back today. No acute issues per caller.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 8 hours as needed for menstrual cramps

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28F, first visit with us. PhD student, came to the area last fall for her program. Last primary care visit was about a year and a half ago at her old office; release signed, records requested.

No complaints today. Feels well. Periods monthly and predictable, crampy the first day or two, takes OTC naproxen 220 mg up to every 8 h on those days and it does the job. Uses condoms. Never pregnant.

PMH: nothing chronic. PSH: none. Meds: naproxen sodium 220 mg PRN cramps only. No supplements. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother has endometriosis. Mother's sister had trouble conceiving. No other family history she knows of.
Social: grad student, lives with a roommate. Never smoked. A drink or two a week, socially. Strict vegetarian for years, no meat or fish; eats a varied plant diet. Walks and bikes to campus.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Pleasant, well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Skin clear. No lymphadenopathy. Mood and affect normal.
PHQ-2 negative.

A/P
- Health maintenance: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids; HIV and hep C screens once, she agreed. Flu and updated COVID shots given in clinic.
- Cervical screening: per her, last Pap 2022 was normal. Will confirm from the records; next due 2025.
- Diet: discussed plant-based nutrition briefly, she is well read on it.
- Back in a year for a physical, or reach me by text for anything before then.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Alyssa, everything from Tuesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. Nice to have you with us.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Received by fax, 14 pages, from the patient's previous primary care practice.

Contents: annual visit notes 2019 through spring 2022, immunization record, labs.
- Problem list: none.
- Medications: naproxen OTC PRN dysmenorrhea.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Cervical cytology 2022: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Routine CBC and metabolic panel 2021: within reference ranges.

Reviewed by PCP. Nothing new; Pap date entered in health maintenance.

events.reason: Painful periods and pain with intercourse

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (400 mg) by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pelvic pain

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Texted last week asking to come in. Since around January her cramps have been getting steadily worse each cycle, now hurting well beyond the first couple of days. Also a deep ache with intercourse that is new over the same stretch. Cycles still regular, roughly monthly, flow unchanged. Has been doubling up: naproxen 220 mg as before plus ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 h as needed for the pelvic pain. Says neither does much anymore. Missed a lab day last month because of it. No fever, no discharge, no urinary symptoms, no bowel changes. Condoms, same partner. Mom has endometriosis and she is worried that is what this is.

O: Vitals in flowsheet. Comfortable. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass, no guarding. Urine hCG negative in office. She would rather have the pelvic exam done by gyn; reasonable.

A/P: Progressive dysmenorrhea with deep dyspareunia, regular cycles, family history in mother. Endometriosis is high on the list.
- Referral to gynecology for evaluation and imaging as they see fit.
- OK to continue the NSAIDs as she is using them, with food; don't take both at the same dose times.
- Will watch for the consult letter.

documents.title: Referral scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Gyn office called back on the referral. First available is Fri 7/12 at 1:20 pm. Let pt know by phone, she is fine with that date and asked to be put on their wait list in case something earlier opens. Referral paperwork sent over.

reports.text:
TRANSVAGINAL PELVIC ULTRASOUND
Indication: dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia.
Technique: transvaginal grayscale and color flow imaging.
Uterus: retroverted, normal in size and contour, homogeneous myometrium. Endometrium thin and uniform for cycle phase.
Right ovary: normal size and appearance, normal follicles, normal flow.
Left ovary: normal size and appearance, normal follicles, normal flow.
Adnexa: no mass. No endometrioma.
Cul-de-sac: no free fluid.

documents.title: Gynecology consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology group
Date of visit: 07/12/2024
Reason for referral: worsening menstrual pain, dyspareunia

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for sending Ms. Rezendes, a 28 year old G0, to see us. For about six months her menstrual pain has climbed cycle by cycle and she now has deep pain with intercourse as well; together they are cutting into her coursework and daily routine. Menses are regular. She has tried ibuprofen and naproxen over the counter without much benefit. Contraception is condoms. Her mother carries a diagnosis of endometriosis and a maternal aunt had infertility. No prior surgery. No drug allergies.

Current medications: naproxen sodium 220 mg every 8 hours as needed for cramps; ibuprofen 400 mg every 6 hours as needed for pelvic pain.

Examination: external genitalia and vagina normal; cervix without lesions. Bimanual exam with a retroverted uterus and tenderness in the posterior cul-de-sac. No adnexal mass palpable.

Labs drawn here: hemoglobin 13.2, WBC 7.5, platelets 250. CA-125 35 U/mL, at the top of our reference range (0-35).
Transvaginal ultrasound today was unremarkable; report attached.

Impression: endometriosis, clinical diagnosis, given the history, the exam and the family history in a patient whose NSAIDs have stopped working. A normal ultrasound does not exclude it.

Plan: we talked through options. First line from here would be hormonal suppression with a continuous combined oral contraceptive; diagnostic laparoscopy is an option if symptoms persist despite that. She would like to hold off on hormones for now and keep using the NSAIDs, and will call us if she wants to start. Happy to see her again at any time.

Allergies: NKDA

Sincerely,
Gynecology

documents.title: Gyn visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Alyssa, I got the letter from gynecology. Sounds like they think this is endometriosis, and the ultrasound and blood count looked fine. They mentioned you'd rather not start the pill right now. That is your call, and the option stays open. How are you doing with the pain this month?

documents.title: RE: Gyn visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks for checking. This month was a bit better honestly. I want to give the ibuprofen/naproxen a few more months before doing anything hormonal. I'll text if it gets bad again.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. 29F.

Interval: saw gyn in July, clinical dx endometriosis, normal TVUS. Declined hormonal suppression for now. Pain since then "about the same," some months tolerable, a day or two each cycle where she uses the ibuprofen and naproxen. Not using them daily between periods. Dyspareunia still there, less frequent. Busy semester, sleeping OK. Mood fine.

Meds: ibuprofen 400 PRN, naproxen 220 PRN. NKDA. Still strict vegetarian. Never smoker, a drink or two weekly.

ROS otherwise negative; no GI upset, no dark stools.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender today. No edema. Skin normal.
PHQ-9: 3.

A/P
1. Endometriosis, managing with as-needed NSAIDs by choice. CBC today given her regular NSAID use and painful cycles. Gyn option reviewed; she knows she can go back.
2. Health maintenance: flu and COVID vaccines given. Pap due next year (last 2022 normal).
3. Physical again next fall.

documents.title: Blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your blood count is normal, no sign of anemia. Good news, nothing further needed.

documents.title: Rough cycle
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, sorry to bug you right before the holiday. This period has been really bad. I'm at my parents' place out of state for break. Could we do a quick video call sometime this week? Any day works, I'm not doing anything.

documents.title: RE: Rough cycle
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not a bother. I'm around Wednesday morning, does 10 work? I'll send the video link.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Telehealth Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video. Pt at her parents' home, out of state; identity confirmed; consents to video.

This cycle started 12/21 and the first three days were the worst she's had since summer. Ibuprofen 400 every 6 h with naproxen at other times took the edge off; today is better. No fever, no vomiting, no black or bloody stools, no stomach pain from the pills. Bleeding not heavier than usual. Not sexually active over break. No urinary symptoms.

Looks comfortable on camera, speaking easily.

A/P: Endometriosis, painful cycle, settling.
- NSAIDs: take with food, stay within label maximums, and don't overlap the two at the same time; stop and call for any black stools or stomach pain.
- Reminded her the gyn's offer of hormonal suppression stands and that laparoscopy is the next step after that if needed. She'll think about calling them after the new year.
- No changes today. Physical due next fall; text me sooner if anything changes.
